2: \label{chap:Picard_QuotScheme}

6: % Grothendieck--Altman--Kleiman Quot-scheme construction
7: % \(\mathrm{Quot}^{\Phi,L}_{E/X/S}\): the per-fiber Hilbert polynomial, the
8: % Quot functor of \(T\)-flat coherent quotients of \(E_T\) on
9: % \(X_T = X \times_S T\), and the Grassmannian \emph{scheme} together with
10: % its representability.
11: %
12: % WHICH ROUTE THIS SERVES. The Quot functor supports the *quotient* route to
13: % Picard representability, via the Hilbert scheme
14: % \(\Hilb_{C/k} = \Quot_{\mathcal{O}_C/C/k}\) -- the case \(E = \mathcal{O}_X\).
15: % That route is not the one being formalised: see
16: % \cref{sec:fga_pic_setup}, which sets it beside the Milne--Kollar route and
17: % explains why the quotient step is the decisive obstruction. This chapter is
18: % retained as the mathematics it is, and its substrate (Grassmannian scheme,
19: % graded algebra, flattening stratification, Hilbert polynomial) is consumed by
20: % the committed route as well, so nothing here is dead material.
21: %
22: % LOAD-BEARING SUB-PREREQUISITE. The Quot construction embeds Quot as a
23: % locally closed subfunctor of a Grassmannian
24: % \(\mathrm{Grass}(W \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_S} \mathrm{Sym}^r V, \Phi(r))\).
25: % Mathlib (at the pinned commit) carries no Grassmannian \emph{scheme} -- only
26: % a linear-algebra Grassmannian as a finite-rank-quotient variety. The
27: % scheme-level Grassmannian over an arbitrary noetherian base is therefore an
28: % in-project sub-build. This chapter introduces it as
29: % \cref{def:grassmannian_scheme} and states its representability
30: % (\cref{thm:grassmannian_representable}).
31: 
32: \section{Setup and motivation}
33: \label{sec:quot_setup}
34: 
35: Throughout this chapter, let \(S\) be a noetherian scheme, \(\pi : X \to S\) a
36: projective morphism, \(L\) a relatively very ample line bundle on \(X\) over \(S\),
37: and \(E\) a coherent sheaf on \(X\). The Quot construction packages the
38: \(T\)-flat coherent quotients \(E_T \twoheadrightarrow \mathcal{F}\) of the
39: pull-back \(E_T\) to \(X_T = X \times_S T\), modulo the equivalence
40: \(\langle \mathcal{F}, q\rangle = \langle \mathcal{F}', q'\rangle\) defined by
41: \(\ker(q) = \ker(q')\). Fixing the Hilbert polynomial
42: \(\Phi(\lambda) = \chi(\mathcal{F}|_{X_t}(\lambda)) \in \mathbb{Q}[\lambda]\)
43: (constant on connected \(T\) by flatness)
44: stratifies the Quot functor into pieces \(\Quot^{\Phi,L}_{E/X/S}\), each of
45: which Grothendieck proved is representable by a projective \(S\)-scheme.
46: This chapter develops the foundations of that picture: the Hilbert
47: polynomial (\cref{def:hilbert_polynomial}), the Quot functor
48: (\cref{def:quot_functor}), and the Grassmannian scheme
49: (\cref{def:grassmannian_scheme}) with its representability
50: (\cref{thm:grassmannian_representable}).

1: \chapter{FGA representability of the Picard scheme}
2: \label{chap:Picard_FGAPicRepresentability}
3: % archon:covers AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/RigidPushforwardGammaBaseChange.lean AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/RigidPushforwardInstance.lean AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/RigidPushforwardP1Topology.lean AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/GaloisDescent/SemilinearAlgebras.lean AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/StableAffineCover.lean
4: 
5: \section{Setup and motivation}
6: \label{sec:fga_pic_setup}
7: 
8: Throughout this chapter, fix a base field \(k\) and a smooth proper geometrically
9: integral curve \(C\) over \(k\) (the curve carrying the Jacobian). The relative
10: Picard presheaf \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k} : (\Sch/k)^{op} \to \Set\) of
11: \cref{chap:Picard_LineBundlePullback} has already been packaged as a
12: set-valued functor and refined to its abelian-group-valued
13: \'etale-sheafified version \(\Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\) in
14: \cref{chap:Picard_RelPicFunctor}. What remains is to produce a scheme
15: representing it: the \emph{Picard scheme} \(\Pic_{C/k}\). The present chapter
16: packages that assembly, together with the abelian-group-scheme refinement.
17: 
18: \medskip
19: 
20: \textbf{Two routes to representability.} The Picard scheme of a curve can be
21: constructed in two ways, and this blueprint records both, because they need
22: different inputs and only one of them is the route under construction here.
23: 
24: The \emph{quotient route} is Grothendieck's, as presented by Kleiman \S 4: the
25: Abel map \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k} \to \Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) exhibits the Picard functor
26: as a quotient of a quasi-projective scheme by a smooth proper equivalence
27: relation, and Altman--Kleiman descent
28: (\cref{lem:smooth_proper_quotient}) represents the quotient. Its engine is the
29: Hilbert scheme \(\Hilb_{C/k} = \Quot_{\mathcal{O}_C/C/k}\) of
30: \cref{chap:Picard_QuotScheme}, whose open subscheme \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\) of
31: relative effective divisors carries the source of the Abel map. This is the route
32: of \cref{thm:fga_pic_representability} and its proof below.
33: 
34: The \emph{Milne--Koll\'ar route} builds \(\Pic^r_{C/k}\) directly, over a
35: separably closed field, from the open loci
36: \[
37:   C^\Sigma = \{\,t : h^0(\mathcal{O}(W - \Sigma)_t) = 1\,\}
38: \]
39: cut out inside a degree-\(r\) divisor scheme by a tuple \(\Sigma\) of rational
40: points, glues them, and descends the result to \(k\) by a finite Galois quotient
41: before assembling the degrees by a coproduct. Its inputs are a rigidified
42: pushforward engine, uniform \(H^1\) vanishing, and Galois descent of rigidified
43: classes --- not a Hilbert or Quot scheme. Its structure, and the parts of it that
44: are established, are the subject of \cref{sec:fga_pic_milne_kollar}.
45: 
46: The decisive difference is the quotient step. Altman--Kleiman descent needs
47: quasi-projectivity of the scheme being quotiented, which is not expressible in
48: the formalisation at present and without which the lemma is false
49: (\cref{rem:smooth_proper_quotient_hypothesis}); the Milne--Koll\'ar route takes
50: only finite Galois quotients under an orbit-in-affine hypothesis, and so avoids
51: that obstruction entirely. The Lean development therefore pursues the
52: Milne--Koll\'ar route. The quotient-route material below is retained as the
53: mathematics it is --- the divisor and Hilbert-scheme substrate it rests on is
54: consumed by both routes --- and is not the path currently being formalised.
55: 
56: \medskip
57: 
58: \textbf{Comparison with the sheafified Picard functor.} Kleiman \S 4 represents
59: the \'etale-sheafified functor \(\Pic_{(C/k)\et}\). This chapter instead
60: works throughout under the standing hypothesis that \emph{\(C\) has a
61: \(k\)-rational point} (\cref{def:has_rational_point}) and states
62: representability against the \emph{plain} relative Picard functor
63: \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) of \cref{def:rel_pic_sharp}. This is justified by
64: Kleiman \S 2, Thm.~2.5 (\texttt{th:comp}): if \(f : X \to S\) has a section
65: and \(\mathcal O_{S'} = f'_* \mathcal O_{X'}\) holds for all base changes
66: (automatic for our proper geometrically integral curve, by cohomology and
67: base change), then the comparison maps
68: \[
69:   \Pic_{X/S}(T) \longrightarrow \Pic_{(X/S)\et}(T) \longrightarrow
70:   \Pic_{(X/S)\fppf}(T)
71: \]
72: are bijective for every \(T\). Hence under the rational-point hypothesis the
73: plain relative functor \emph{is} the \'etale sheaf, so the rational point
74: allows us to work directly with \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\).
75: 
76: The hypothesis is not a convenience: without a section the plain functor is not
77: even a Zariski sheaf in general, so a representability statement for
78: \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) with no rational point would be false. Two honest
79: formulations are therefore available, and they prove different theorems.
80: 
81: \begin{enumerate}
82:   \item Represent \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) and carry \(C(k) \neq \emptyset\) as a
83:     hypothesis. This is the formulation of
84:     \cref{thm:fga_pic_representability} and of every representability assertion
85:     in this chapter. It is strictly weaker than a statement about all smooth
86:     proper geometrically integral curves, since such a curve need not have a
87:     rational point --- a conic without rational points, or a genus-\(2\) curve
88:     over \(\mathbb{Q}\) with no rational point, satisfies every other
89:     hypothesis.
90:   \item Represent the \'etale sheafification \(\Pic_{(C/k)\et}\) and drop the
91:     rational point. This is Kleiman's own formulation, and needs no section
92:     precisely because sheafifying supplies \'etale-locally what the section
93:     would have supplied globally. It requires developing the Picard functor on
94:     the \'etale site.
95: \end{enumerate}
96: 
97: Which formulation the project should target is a decision about what theorem is
98: being claimed, not a limitation of the platform. The two are recorded here
99: side by side; the chapter as written realises the first.
100: 
101: Every representability assertion of this chapter accordingly carries the
102: rational-point hypothesis. A pointed curve \((C,P)\), as in
103: \cref{chap:AbelJacobi}, supplies such a section.
104: 
105: % SOURCE: [Kleiman], ``The Picard scheme'', \S 4 (FGA Explained Ch.~9 \S 9.4);
106: % arXiv:math/0504020, p.~26. Read from
107: % references/kleiman-picard-src/kleiman-picard.tex.
108: 
109: \section{Line bundles and the Quot / Hilbert scheme}
110: \label{sec:fga_pic_line_bundle_quot}
111: 
112: The bridge from line bundles on \(C \times_k T\) to the Quot scheme is the
113: Abel map: a relative effective divisor \(D \subset C \times_k T\) over \(T\)
114: (a \(T\)-flat closed subscheme whose ideal is invertible) determines a closed
115: subscheme of \(C \times_k T\) flat over \(T\), hence a \(T\)-point of the Hilbert
116: functor \(\Hilb_{C/k}(T)\), which is the special case \(\Quot_{\mathcal{O}_C/C/k}\)
117: of the Quot functor of \cref{chap:Picard_QuotScheme}; and it determines an
118: invertible sheaf \(\mathcal{O}_{C \times_k T}(D)\) on the relative curve,
119: representing a class in \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}(T)\).
120: 
121: \begin{definition}[Abel-map witness]\leanok
122:   \label{def:abel_map_witness}
123:   \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.PicScheme.abelMapWitness}
124:   \uses{def:div_functor_carrier, def:pic_sharp_carrier}
125:   Let \(C/k\) be a smooth proper curve. Define a
126:   natural transformation
127:   \[
128:     A^{\mathrm{raw}}_{C/k} \colon \mathrm{Div}_{C/k}
129:       \longrightarrow \Pic^\sharp_{C/k}
130:   \]
131:   as the composite
132:   \(
133:     \mathrm{abelKernelNatTrans}(C)
134:     \mathbin{;} \mathrm{picNeg}(C)
135:   \).
136: \end{definition}
137: 
138: \begin{proof}\leanok
139:   The first transformation sends the class represented by
140:   \(\langle \mathcal F,q\rangle\) to \([\ker q]\). It is well defined because
141:   equivalent divisor families induce isomorphic kernels. It is natural under
142:   arbitrary base change because the kernel--pullback comparison is an
143:   isomorphism for an epimorphic quotient with finitely presented, base-flat
144:   target and invertible kernel. The second transformation is pointwise
145:   inversion in the group-valued presheaf \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\). Their composite
146:   is therefore natural and sends
147:   \(\langle \mathcal F,q\rangle\) to \(-[\ker q]\).
148: \end{proof}
149: 
150: \begin{lemma}[Line bundle / Quot correspondence via the Abel map]\leanok
151:   \label{lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence}
152:   \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.PicScheme.abelMap_app_mk}
153:   \uses{def:abel_map_witness, def:inst_has_abel_map, def:has_abel_map,
154:     def:div_functor_carrier, def:pic_sharp_carrier}
155:   % SOURCE: [Kleiman], ``The Picard scheme'', \S 3, Def.~dfn:Abel (the Abel
156:   % map), and Thm.~th:repDiv (representability of relative effective
157:   % divisors by an open subscheme of \(\IHilb_{X/S}\)); arXiv:math/0504020,
158:   % pp.~25, 23 (read from
159:   % references/kleiman-picard-src/kleiman-picard.tex, L1837-L1841 + L2135-L2145).
160:   % Source identifiers: \begin{thm}\label{th:repDiv}\end{thm}
161:   % and \begin{dfn}\label{dfn:Abel}\end{dfn}.
162:   \textit{Source: [Kleiman], ``The Picard scheme'', \S 3,
163:   Thm.~3.7 + Def.~4.6 (cf.\ [Nitsure], ``Construction of Hilbert
164:   and Quot Schemes'', \S 1, where \(\Hilb_{X/S} = \Quot_{\mathcal{O}_X/X/S}\)).}
165:   Let \(C/k\) be a smooth proper geometrically integral curve. There is a
166:   natural transformation of presheaves on \((\Sch/k)^{op}\)
167:   \[
168:     A_{C/k} = \mathrm{abelMap} \;\colon\; \mathrm{Div}_{C/k}
169:       \;\longrightarrow\; \Pic^\sharp_{C/k}
170:   \]
171:   (\(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\) the relative-divisor functor of
172:   \cref{def:div_functor_carrier}, \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) the relative
173:   Picard functor of \cref{def:pic_sharp_carrier}), with the following
174:   \emph{defining property}: at a \(T\)-point represented by a family
175:   \(\langle \mathcal F, q\rangle\) (\cref{def:div_family}: a finitely
176:   presented, \(T\)-flat quotient
177:   \(q \colon \mathcal O_{C\times_kT}\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal F\)
178:   whose kernel is an invertible ideal sheaf cutting out a relative effective
179:   divisor \(D\subseteq C\times_kT\)),
180:   \[
181:     A_{C/k}(T)\bigl(\langle \mathcal F, q\rangle\bigr)
182:       \;=\; -[\ker q] \;=\; [(\ker q)^{-1}]
183:       \;=\; \bigl[\mathcal{O}_{C \times_k T}(D)\bigr]
184:       \;\in\; \Pic^\sharp_{C/k}(T),
185:   \]
186:   the class of the associated invertible sheaf \(\mathcal{O}_{C \times_k
187:   T}(D)\), i.e.\ the additive inverse of the class of the ideal sheaf
188:   \(\ker q\) (Kleiman \S 3, Def.~dfn:Abel). This transformation is the
189:   required witness for \(\mathrm{HasAbelMap}(C)\)
190:   (\cref{def:has_abel_map}).
191: \end{lemma}
192: 
193: \begin{proof}
194:   The instance of \cref{def:inst_has_abel_map} identifies
195:   \(A_{C/k}\) with the witness of \cref{def:abel_map_witness}. Evaluating its
196:   two factors at \(\langle \mathcal F,q\rangle\) first gives the kernel class
197:   \([\ker q]\) and then its inverse. Since the kernel is the ideal sheaf of
198:   \(D\), its inverse is \(\mathcal O_{C\times_kT}(D)\), which gives the stated
199:   formula.
200: \end{proof}
201: 
202: \begin{remark}
203: [Representability of \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\)]
204:   \label{rem:div_functor_representability}
205:   Kleiman~\S 3, Thm.~th:repDiv, shows that \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\) is
206:   representable by an open subscheme \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k} \subseteq
207:   \Hilb_{C/k}\) of the Hilbert scheme (\(\Hilb_{C/k} =
208:   \Quot_{\mathcal{O}_C/C/k}\), \cref{chap:Picard_QuotScheme}): letting
209:   \(W \subseteq C \times_k \Hilb_{C/k}\) be the universal closed
210:   subscheme and \(q \colon W \to \Hilb_{C/k}\) the projection, the locus
211:   \(V \subseteq W\) where \(W\) is locally an effective Cartier divisor
212:   is open, so \(Z := q(W \setminus V)\) is closed (\(q\) proper) and
213:   \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k} := \Hilb_{C/k} \setminus Z\) is the open
214:   subscheme representing relative effective divisors. This is
215:   the relative-divisor functor appearing in
216:   \cref{def:div_functor_carrier}.
217: \end{remark}
218: 
219: \section{The FGA representability theorem}
220: \label{sec:fga_pic_representability}
221: 
222: We now state and prove the specialisation of Grothendieck's existence theorem
223: for the Picard scheme, in the specialisation needed for the Jacobian:
224: \(S = \Spec k\), \(X = C\) a smooth proper geometrically integral
225: curve. The general theorem (Kleiman \S 4, Thm.~4.8) covers any
226: \(X/S\) projective Zariski-locally over \(S\), flat, with integral geometric
227: fibers; we record the general statement and then specialise.
228:

230:   \label{thm:fga_pic_representability}

229: \begin{theorem}[FGA representability of the Picard scheme]\leanok
230:   \label{thm:fga_pic_representability}
231:   \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.PicScheme.representable}
232:   \uses{lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence, lem:smooth_proper_quotient,
233:         thm:quot_representable, def:rel_pic_sharp, def:has_rational_point,
234:         cor:flattening_stratification_curve, def:pic_sharp_representable,
235:         def:inst_pic_sharp_representable, lem:cech_flat_base_change}
242:   \textit{Source: [Kleiman], ``The Picard scheme'', \S 4, Main Thm.~4.8
243:   + Cor.~4.18.3.}
244:   Let \(k\) be a field and \(C\) a smooth proper geometrically integral curve
245:   over \(k\) \emph{with a \(k\)-rational point}
246:   (\cref{def:has_rational_point}). Then the relative Picard functor
247:   \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) of \cref{def:rel_pic_sharp} --- which under the
248:   rational-point hypothesis coincides with its \'etale sheafification
249:   \(\Pic_{(C/k)\et}\), by Kleiman \S 2, Thm.~2.5 --- is representable by a
250:   \(k\)-scheme \(\Pic_{C/k}\), separated and locally of finite type over
251:   \(k\), which is a disjoint union of open quasi-projective
252:   \(k\)-subschemes, each an increasing union of open quasi-projective
253:   subschemes. The scheme \(\Pic_{C/k}\) is called the \emph{Picard scheme}
254:   of \(C/k\).
255: \end{theorem}
256: 
257: \begin{proof}
258:   
259:   We follow Kleiman~\S 4, Thm.~4.8, specialised to \(S = \Spec k\) and
260:   \(X = C\). The proof proceeds in four conceptual steps, preceded by a
261:   comparison step; the underlying algebraic engine is the Quot scheme of
262:   \cref{chap:Picard_QuotScheme} and the relative Picard functor of
263:   \cref{chap:Picard_RelPicFunctor}, together with the line-bundle / Quot
264:   correspondence of \cref{lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence}.
265: 
266:   \emph{Step 0: reduce to the \'etale sheaf via the rational point.}
267:   By Kleiman \S 2, Thm.~2.5, since \(C \to \Spec k\) has a section
268:   (\cref{def:has_rational_point}) and \(\mathcal O_T = \pi_{T*}
269:   \mathcal O_{C \times_k T}\) holds for every \(k\)-scheme \(T\) (cohomology
270:   and base change for the proper geometrically integral fibers of
271:   \(C\times_k T/T\)), the comparison map
272:   \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}(T) \to \Pic_{(C/k)\et}(T)\) is bijective for all
273:   \(T\). It therefore suffices to represent the \'etale sheaf
274:   \(\Pic_{(C/k)\et}\), which is what Kleiman's theorem produces; the same
275:   scheme then represents \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\).
276: 
277:   \emph{Step 1: stratify by Hilbert polynomial.}
278:   For each polynomial \(\phi \in \mathbb{Q}[n]\), let \(P^\phi \subseteq
279:   \Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\) be the \'etale subsheaf whose \(T\)-points are
280:   represented by invertible sheaves \(\mathcal{L}\) on \(C \times_k T\) with
281:   \(\chi(C_t, \mathcal{L}_t^{-1}(n)) = \phi(n)\) for all \(t \in T\) (the
282:   Hilbert polynomial relative to the chosen polarisation
283:   \(\mathcal{O}_C(1)\) on the projective curve \(C\)). The \(P^\phi\) form a
284:   disjoint open cover of \(\Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\) (openness via Kleiman's
285:   flat-base-change argument, \cref{lem:cech_flat_base_change} / Stacks Tag 02KH;
286:   cf.\ EGA III 7.9.11). It suffices to
287:   represent each \(P^\phi\) by an increasing union of open quasi-projective
288:   \(k\)-schemes.
289: 
290:   \emph{Step 2: bound twists by \(m\)-regularity.}
291:   Given \(\phi\), fix \(m\) large enough that the \(T\)-points of \(P^\phi\) are
292:   representable by \(\mathcal{L}\) on \(C \times_k T\) satisfying
293:   \(R^i \pi_{T*} \mathcal{L}(n) = 0\) for all \(i \ge 1\), \(n \ge m\). Twisting
294:   by \(\mathcal{O}_C(m)\) defines an automorphism of \(\Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\)
295:   that carries \(P^\phi\) to \(P^{\phi_0}_0\) for \(\phi_0(n) := \phi(m + n)\).
296:   Hence it suffices to represent each \(P^{\phi_0}_0\) by a quasi-projective
297:   \(k\)-scheme.
298: 
299:   \emph{Step 3: factor through the Abel map.}
300:   Consider the Abel map \(A_{C/k} : \mathrm{Div}_{C/k} \to \Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\)

===== AbelJacobi intro
1: \chapter{The Abel--Jacobi map}
2: \label{chap:AbelJacobi}
3: 
4: Let \(C\) be a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve over a field \(k\),
5: let \(P \in C(k)\), and let \(\Jac(C)\) be the Albanese variety constructed in
6: Chapter~\ref{chap:Jacobian}.  This chapter records the universal morphism and its
7: two defining properties.
8: 
9: \section{Definition}
10: 
11: \begin{definition}[Abel--Jacobi map]\leanok
12:   \label{def:ofCurve}
13:   \uses{def:Jacobian, def:IsAlbanese, def:IsAlbanese_ofCurve,
14:     thm:nonempty_jacobianWitness}
15:   \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.ofCurve}
16:   The \emph{Abel--Jacobi map at \(P\)} is the universal pointed morphism
17:   \[
18:     \alpha_P \colon C \longrightarrow \Jac(C)
19:   \]
20:   supplied by the Albanese property of \(\Jac(C)\).
21: \end{definition}
22: 
23: \begin{remark}
24: [Picard description]
25:   \label{rem:ofCurve_classical}
26:   Under the identification \(\Jac(C) = \Pic^0_{C/k}\), the morphism is
27:   \[
28:     \alpha_P(Q) = [\mathcal O_C(Q-P)].
29:   \]
30:   Equivalently, it is classified by
31:   \(\mathcal O_{C\times C}(\Delta-p_1^*P)\), regarded as a family of
32:   degree-zero line bundles over the second factor.
33: \end{remark}
34:

36:

1: # Algebraic Jacobian Challenge
2: 
3: A Lean 4 formalization of the Jacobian of a smooth, proper, geometrically
4: irreducible curve over a field.  The project takes the Picard-scheme route: build
5: the relative Picard functor, represent it, identify its identity component as an
6: abelian variety of dimension the genus, and derive the Albanese universal
7: property.  The first and last legs are substantially built; representability is
8: the open frontier.
9: 
10: Representability is being built by the **Milne–Kollár route** — construct
11: `Pic^r` over a separably closed field from the loci where `h⁰ = 1`, glue,
12: descend to `k` by a finite Galois quotient, assemble the degrees by a coproduct.
13: The plan of record is [`informal/pic-representability-campaign.md`](informal/pic-representability-campaign.md).
14: The Grothendieck/Kleiman quotient route via the Quot scheme is **not** the path
15: being built: its descent step needs a quasi-projectivity hypothesis that is not
16: expressible at the pinned Mathlib revision and without which the lemma is false.
17: Its substrate (Grassmannians, graded algebra, flattening stratification) is
18: sorry-free and is consumed by the committed route, so it is retained.
19: 
20: Two of the committed route's own engines are substantially built.  The rigidified
21: pushforward gate is **discharged**: `Adelic.instHasRigidPushforwardOfCurve` is a real
22: instance for every curve satisfying the challenge hypotheses, and it measures axiom-clean
23: at the synthesis site, as do the three extraction theorems that now synthesise it rather
24: than assuming it.  The finite Galois
25: quotient has Speiser descent, the affine quotient, and `Γ`-stable affine covers proved;
26: what remains there is gluing.  Both are stated with proofs and Lean pins in the
27: blueprint's FGA chapter, §"The Milne–Kollár route".  Neither route is hypothesis-free:
28: the quotient route needs quasi-projectivity of the Abel-map slice, the committed route
29: needs every finite Galois orbit to lie in an affine open, and the same Hironaka example
30: defeats both if its hypothesis is dropped.  The difference is that the orbit condition is
31: available for the schemes this route quotients.
32: 
33: It is developed alongside `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild`, which attacks the
34: same theorem by a separate curve-specialized strategy.

/-! ## §2. The Abel map — line-bundle / Quot correspondence

The bridge from line bundles on `C ×_k T` to the Quot scheme is the **Abel
map**: a relative effective divisor `D ⊆ C ×_k T` over `T` determines a
`T`-point of `Div_{C/k}`, and the dual ideal sheaf
`O_{C ×_k T}(D) := I_D⁻¹` represents a class in `Pic^♯_{C/k}(T)`.

Blueprint reference: `lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence` (Kleiman §3
Def. `dfn:Abel` + Thm. `th:repDiv`). -/
/-- Existence instance for `PicSharpRepresentable`: `PicScheme C` is
`Classical.choose` of the `HasPicScheme` existential, and the first component
of `Exists.choose_spec` says precisely that the chosen scheme represents
`picSharp C` (the remaining components are local finiteness and
separatedness). The FGA content lives upstream in `instHasPicScheme`. -/
instance instPicSharpRepresentable {k : Type u} [Field k]
    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] [HasPicScheme C] : PicSharpRepresentable C :=
  ⟨(HasPicScheme.has_pic_scheme (C := C)).choose_spec.1⟩

/-- **FGA representability of the Picard scheme.**

Let `k` be a field and `C` a smooth proper geometrically integral curve over
`k` (with, through the `HasPicScheme` hypothesis chain, a `k`-rational
point). Then the relative Picard functor `Pic^♯_{C/k}` is representable by
the Picard scheme `PicScheme C`: there is a natural bijection

```
(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)
```

for every `k`-scheme `T`. This `RepresentableBy` structure is a comparison
against the relative Picard functor itself, so downstream consumers
(tangent-space computation at the identity, `Pic⁰` degree theory) can compose
with its `homEquiv` to transfer line-bundle data to scheme points. -/
